Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. We have leadership buy-in to pilot Redwood Dedicated but one hard requirement: all inference traffic and model state for the pilot must remain within Canada (data residency + bank policy). Montreal is our preferred region.

High-level asks:
- Dedicated pool physically in Canada (Montreal preferred) with SOC2 evidence and KMS integration.
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~120 qps of low-latency chat generation across 3 endpoints (customer support, fraud detection enrichment, knowledge search).
- Typical request: 1.2k tokens in / out average per session, ~2M tokens/day initially. Peak concurrency estimated 350 simultaneous streams during business-hours spikes.
- Target latency: p50 <= 80ms token, p99 <= 450ms token for the primary chat model.

We are at the stage to scope capacity and get a draft SOW. Can you put together a proposed node count, lead times, and a simple cost estimate? Also include any networking/VPC requirements we need to plan for with our infra team.

Emily

Vanessa / Karthik / Emily — draft calc below and assumptions up front.

Assumptions:
- Model: 13B-class optimized for chat (quantized 4-bit TF/INT8-ish profile) as primary. Fallback to 33B quantized for high-quality responses 10% of requests.
- Avg tokens/request: 1.2k roundtrip as Emily noted. Tokenization and batching efficiencies of ~12% expected with KV caching for repeated prefixes.
- Target sustained qps: 120, peak concurrency 350. We budget for a 1.6x safety buffer -> design for 560 concurrent streams for headroom.

Node options and throughput (baseline estimates):
- A100 80GB (single-node serving): ~220 concurrent 13B streams; 90 qps sustained for typical chat.
- H100 80GB: ~350 concurrent 13B streams; 150 qps sustained.

Preliminary sizing (to meet p99 goals with redundancy and rolling maintenance):
- Option A (cost-conscious): 4 x A100 nodes (usable capacity ~880 concurrent streams, sustained ~360 qps). Redundancy: N+1.
- Option B (latency-first / headroom): 3 x H100 nodes (usable capacity ~1,050 concurrent streams after small overhead, sustained ~450 qps). Redundancy: N. Recommend 4 x H100 if we want N+1.

Notes on networking/compliance:
- Private VPC peering + egress controls; customer-managed firewall rules.
- KMS: we support Bring-Your-Own-KMS (HSM-backed) with key policies limited to Canada region.
- Audit logs: per-token tracing disabled by default; we can provide request-level traces and policy-approved logs for SOC2. Retention configurable for up to 3 years.

Lead times:
- A100 fleet in Montreal (partner DC): ~6-8 weeks procurement + rack + networking provisioning.
- H100 procurement: ~10-12 weeks if customer requests guaranteed H100 hardware.

Suggested nearterm ask: propose Option B with 4 x H100 (N+1) but indicate Option A as cost alternative. Attach capacity calc sheet (I will add numbers).

I'll attach the spreadsheet and a short SOW bullet list for Karthik to convert to contract language.

-Soojin
Soojin Lee
Infrastructure Capacity, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — a few procurement and contract notes to include in the SOW draft:

1) Pricing model: propose 12-month reserved capacity with a 60% commitment on baseline throughput and a burstable overlay for 30% of peak months. This keeps pricing predictable given MapleBank wants dedicated compute.

2) SLA / failover language: define maintenance windows and a cross-region fallback plan (we can route non-residency-sensitive traffic to our primary US pool if customer signs a waiver). For MapleBank pilot, no cross-border fallback allowed without explicit auth — call this out.

3) Lead times & payment: initial deployment deposit to start procurement (50% of first 3 months), remainder invoiced on deployment. Add 8-week calendar float for customs/shipping to Montreal.

4) Compliance pack: we can provide SOC2 Type II report, HSM logos, and a compliance attestation for data residency. Also note we need a brief network config checklist filled out by MapleBank's networking team (I will attach).

Vanessa — I'll draft a short SOW (1.5 pages) reflecting Option B as default and Option A as cost alternative; include an explicit "No cross-border fallback" clause for the pilot.

-Karthik
